Compare identity and optimal fits on the same observations without treating either as uniformly more efficient. Inspect support reasons ([Section 7](#fitted-support)) separately from covariance regularization: the former concerns available effects, while the latter concerns the weighting of valid comparison moments.

## 15. Execution Options, Custom Estimators and Supported Limits {#guide-15}

Keep ordinary exploration serial. If multiplier products become the expensive step, `pl = TRUE, cores = 2` requires the matching `control = list(workers = 2)`. Only the multiplier products run in parallel; estimation stays serial, and worker buffers count toward the same workspace. Signs are drawn in the calling session. This optional call is shown but excluded from rendering so the guide does not start worker processes automatically.

```{r}
#| label: optional-parallel-multiplier
#| eval: false
set.seed(20261104)
fit_parallel <- cdid::att_gt(
  yname = "y", tname = "time", idname = "id", gname = "g",
  xformla = ~ x + z, data = balanced_panel, frame = units,
  control_group = "nevertreated", est_method = "dr", selection = "none",
  pt_assumption = "post", bstrap = TRUE, cband = TRUE, biters = bootstrap_draws,
  pl = TRUE, cores = 2L,
  control = list(workers = 2L, numeric_workspace_bytes = workspace_bytes)
)
summary(fit_parallel)
```

A custom `est_method` is a callable IPW implementation with the documented signature `f(y1, y0, D, covariates, i.weights, inffunc = TRUE, ...)`. It must return a finite scalar `ATT` and `att.inf.func` with one entry per supplied row, in order, including the correct nuisance-estimation contribution. The supplied weights already incorporate the route's response-rate adjustment. Under conditional observation weighting, it must additionally provide `log_weight_gradient`, the derivative of ATT with respect to each supplied log weight. Shape checks do not establish that the mathematics is valid. This guide uses the built-in estimators; a full custom implementation is a separate development task, documented in [Treatment adjustment](https://github.com/dvbn/cdid/blob/main/docs/methods/treatment.md).

| Entry point | Current supported boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `selection_est_method = "dr"` | Requires built-in `est_method = "dr"`; imputation and augmented routes require `"F"` and no transport ratio. |
| Custom IPW callbacks | Baseline and qualified observation weighting only; no imputation or augmented callback route. |
| Genuine repeated cross sections | `panel = FALSE` selects ordinary `did` delegation; chained mode requires within-unit changes. Dependent rows from this panel are not an IID repeated-cross-section example. |
| GMM covariance handling | `"tikhonov"` is supported; Moore-Penrose weighting is deferred and refused. |
| Per-fit accuracy guarantees | `control$relative_accuracy` is refused; current numerical checks do not provide a guaranteed error certificate. |

**What to inspect and try changing:** Use [Options](https://github.com/dvbn/cdid/blob/main/docs/reference/options.md) to match a supported combination before adding an option. Try `print_details = TRUE` on an existing serial call. Read recorded inference and support statuses rather than assuming a completed fit verifies the scientific assumptions.

## 16. Save Results and Choose Your Next Experiment {#guide-16}

The following optional chunk writes only to the clearly named `guide-output/` folder under the project root: a cell table, dynamic table, plot, and serialized fit. It is excluded from automatic rendering; run it deliberately when you want files. `saveRDS()` preserves the fitted result for later `readRDS()` in a compatible package environment ([Saving and exporting](https://github.com/dvbn/cdid/blob/main/docs/reference/results.md#saving-and-exporting)).

```{r}
#| label: optional-export
#| eval: false
output_dir <- file.path(proj_root, "guide-output")
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
utils::write.csv(cdid::tidy(fit_bal), file.path(output_dir, "balanced-cells.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(cdid::tidy(agg_bal_dynamic), file.path(output_dir, "balanced-dynamic.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "balanced-dynamic.png"),
  plot = cdid::ggdid(agg_bal_dynamic), width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 150)
saveRDS(fit_bal, file.path(output_dir, "balanced-fit.rds"))
```

Use this workflow for an experiment:

1. **Change the DGP:** Edit `cfg` in [Section 2](#guide-2), redraw once, inspect study units, truth benchmarks, and raw missingness/pair counts ([Section 3](#guide-3)), and rerun every downstream fit using that draw. Keep failures; do not search seeds until an estimator succeeds.
2. **Change only an estimator:** Keep the same data and study-unit table `frame = units`, edit a visible `att_gt()` call, and refit. Rebuild its `aggte()` objects so a comparison never uses stale summaries.
3. **Interpret the output:** Compare the correctly defined target with estimates and 6-decimal uncertainty; inspect model, support ([Section 7](#fitted-support)), pretrend ([Section 11](#guide-11)), and GMM ([Section 14](#guide-14)) records. One draw cannot establish repeated-sample performance.
4. **Change inference:** Match the dependence structure, significance level, band family, and multiplier seed/count ([Section 10](#guide-10)). Restart R after package reinstalls, then rerun setup and the required chunks.

**Try changing:** Choose one parameter, such as `effect_x` or `obs_x_slope`, write down the predicted change before redrawing, and compare that prediction with the visible output without altering the draw afterward.

### Navigation and Function Map {#function-map}

| Section | Practical task | Functions and main controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [1. Setup](#guide-1) | Check loaded versions and paths | `packageVersion()`, `find.package()`, `source()` |
| [2. DGP](#guide-2) | Edit one config, draw study units, inspect superpopulation vs study-unit truth | `default_dgp_config()`, `simulate_panel()` |
| [3. Missingness exploration](#guide-3) | Inspect zero/singleton/repeat counts and pair support before fitting | `aggregate()`, `table()`, selected pairs, `study_units` denominators |
| [4. First fit](#guide-4) | Balanced-panel cells, all four aggregations, and plots | `att_gt()`, `summary()`, `tidy()`, `glance()`, `aggte()`, `ggdid()` |
| [5. Missing outcomes](#guide-5) | Define `selection_universe = "F"` and `selection_pooling = "separate"`, compare pair and date logits | `selection`, `selection_model`, `selection_universe`, `selection_pooling`, `frame` |
| [6. Treatment adjustment](#guide-6) | Refit IPW, OR, and DR on the same draw with distinct `selection_xformla` | `est_method`, `xformla`, `selection_xformla` |
| [7. Pooling, rotation, and support](#guide-7) | Shared slopes, date independence vs study-unit retention, rotating windows, and fitted `tidy()` support | `selection_pooling`, `selection_universe`, `tidy()`, `chained$frame` |
| [8. Reconstruct changes](#guide-8) | Compare observation weighting, change imputation, and augmented double-DR | `selection_est_method`, `imputation_pooling` |
| [9. Controls and PT](#guide-9) | NT/NYT, preperiod reporting, `PT-all`, and ordinary `did` delegation | `control_group`, `base_period`, `pt_assumption`, `pt_start`, `mode` |
| [10. Inference](#guide-10) | Pointwise intervals, multiplier bands, and actual clustering | `bstrap`, `cband`, `biters`, `clustervars` |
| [11. Pretrends](#guide-11) | Full Wald and conditional CvM pretrend records | `chained$pretest`, `conditional_did_pretest()` |
| [12. Robustness](#guide-12) | Three continuous-$X$ cases testing $p$ and $m$ misspecification separately | Shared `xformla`, `est_method = "dr"`, `"reg"`, `"ipw"` |
| [13. References and weights](#guide-13) | Dated $X$, first-period vs base-period weight laws | `weightsname`, `fix_weights` |
| [14. Diagnostics](#guide-14) | GMM weighting, resource caps, and point-only limits | `gmm_weighting`, `control`, `compute_inffunc` |
| [15. Extensions](#guide-15) | Optional parallel multiplier call and custom callback contract | `pl`, `cores`, `control$workers`, callable `est_method` |
| [16. Save and iterate](#guide-16) | Optional exports and structured experiment workflow | `write.csv()`, `ggsave()`, `saveRDS()` |
